findings.claim: Every new attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. As a result, generated code compiled for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework gets no `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` at all. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists on both (.NET Framework 4.0+ and .NET Standard 2.0) and can be applied to classes, so the exclusion is not needed for compilation. It breaks the 'All generated code is decorated' criterion for a very common class of consumers (netstandard2.0 libraries, net472 apps). The README states the wrong availability claim as fact.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageDownlevelTargetsTests.GeneratedTypes_AreExcludedFromCodeCoverage_OnDownlevelTargets with InlineData NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK. On head the generated formatter and resolver symbols carry no ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute, although the attribute type resolves.

findings.claim: CompositeResolverTemplate emits the attribute unconditionally and ignores the new opt-out. The README says the opt-out `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver(ExcludeFromCodeCoverage = false)]` applies to 'all generated formatters and resolvers', but a generated composite resolver stays decorated with no way to opt out.

receipt_plan.detail: CompositeResolverTemplate.tt lines 7-9 and 35-37 have no `if (Options.Generator.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage)` guard, unlike ResolverTemplate.tt and FormatterTemplate.tt. Compare with the README line 'To opt out, set [GeneratedMessagePackResolver(ExcludeFromCodeCoverage = false)]'.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Decorate generated formatters and resolvers by default and add a public opt-out. The change adds `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage { get; set; } = true` with PublicAPI entries, `GeneratorOptions.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`, and `is not false` parsing in AnalyzerUtilities. The Formatter, StringKey, Enum, Union and Resolver templates guard emission with `if (Options.Generator.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage)`.

interpretations.summary: Decorate all generated code unconditionally with no new setting or public API, as the requester said 'I do not feel like a setting is needed'. Starting from this change: remove the attribute property and its four PublicAPI.Unshipped entries, the GeneratorOptions property, and the AnalyzerUtilities assignment. Drop the `<# if (Options.Generator.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage) { #>` guards so the templates always emit the attribute, as CompositeResolverTemplate already does. Remove the README opt-out sentence.
